newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Tamil parties say government appointed coordinating committee for northeast province is an eyewash. Eelam People's Democratic Party and People's Liberation Organisation of Tamil Eelam refuse to participate in it.
Three hundred and eighty Tamil refugees land in Rameshwaram in south India during last two days from Mannar, in northwestern Sri Lanka.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga appoints coordinating council to oversee programme to accelerate food production drive. Plan is to raise rice production to the level of self-sufficiency. President proposes tariff and fiscal concessions to attract foreign investment into agriculture.
High court orders arrest of wife of deputy fisheries minister Milroy Fernando and three others convicted of murder.
Tamil Tiger rebels massacre 11 civilians, wound 27, in attack on bus in Aranthalawa. Ten seriously wounded victims airlifted to hospital.
Security forces repulse Tamil Tiger rebel attack on defences in Vavuniya, killing two rebels and recovering their bodies along with arms.
President Kumaratunga tells Agriculture Ministry to accelerate food production drive and transform uneconomic paddy fields into other productive uses.
